note: 📡️ The status of a history change that replays before this replica adopts it (ticket 26/09/30/NON-DESTRUCTIVE-HISTORY-EDITING design §16.6, §20.8, gap N17; audit W1E-3): every shell announces `text` in a polite status region outside the History panel (React `[data-semio-history-reprojection]`, wgpu mirror key `shell.history.reprojection`) and the history body titles its `framework.history.reprojection` section with `title`. A refused adoption (a fault with nothing left to replay) reads `<kind>.refused` with the fault's placeholder-free history notice, else `reason.unnamed`; a paused remote change reads `remote.paused` (a step or a load is never paused); anything else its kind's progress (a fault while operations remain keeps the progress line). An absent kind is `remote`. The Rust kernel (`HISTORY_REPROJECTION_LABELS`, `history_reprojection_status`) and its TypeScript twin carry exactly these rows and read every case to its status.
